title: Which digits hide behind the letters in this sum?
description: A column addition has letters in place of digits. The video starts with the units column to find B, carries one, and then uses the tens column to find A. Keeko doubts the tens column and forgets the carry, and the video shows why the sum then breaks.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a letter sum, work from the units column and carry into the tens column. Watch for students who add the tens column without the carried one.

video_script.why: The child adds two digit numbers easily and now reads the addition backwards to find hidden digits.
video_script.substitution: Solve the units column first, note the carry, then solve the tens column with the carry included.
video_script.anchor: the cryptarithm A1 + 1B = B0 of the book, drawn as a column addition
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tens column without the carried one, so A + 1 = 9 and A = 8. Then 81 + 19 = 100, not 90.
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh is seven and B is nine.

final_answer.spoken: eigh is seven and B is nine

maths_rules: A1 + 1B = B0, with A and B different digits
units column: 1 + B ends in 0, and B is at most 9, so 1 + B = 10, B = 9, carry 1
tens column: A + 1 + 1 = B = 9, so A = 9 - 2 = 7
Keeko without the carry: A + 1 = 9, A = 8; 81 + 19 = 100, not 90
video_script.design: One cryptarithm drawn as a column addition. Units first, then the carry into the tens. Wrong idea: forgetting the carry.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='puzzle'/>It is a puzzle where each letter stands for a digit, and it is called a cryptarithm.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum is eigh one plus one B, and it makes B zero.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which digits are hiding behind eigh and B?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Each letter hides one digit, and different letters hide different digits.
<bookmark mark='first'/>A number never begins with zero.
<bookmark mark='cols'/>We add the units column first, and then the tens column.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>If a column makes ten or more, we write the units digit and carry one.

beats.on_screen: Given: A1 + 1B = B0, A and B are different digits

marks.given: the line Given: A1 + 1B = B0 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh one plus one B equals B zero, and eigh and B are different digits.

beats.on_screen: To find: the digits A and B

marks.find: the line To find: the digits A and B is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the digits eigh and B.

beats.on_screen: Units column: 1 + B must end in 0, so 1 + B = 10, B = 9, carry 1

marks.ends: the line 1 + B ends in 0 is written
marks.nine: 1 + B = 10, B = 9 and the carry 1 are written

beats.colours: the units column in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step one, add the units column, because we always start there.
<bookmark mark='ends'/>One plus B must end in zero, and B is a single digit.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>That makes one plus B equal to ten, so B is nine, and we carry one.

beats.on_screen: Tens column: A + 1 + 1 = B = 9, so A = 9 - 2 = 7

marks.tens: the tens column is lit and the carried 1 is added

beats.colours: the tens column in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Step two, add the tens column with the carried one, because it belongs there.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Eigh plus one plus one must give the tens digit of the answer. That digit is B, and B is nine.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Eigh plus two equals nine, and nine take away two is seven.

beats.on_screen: Check: 71 + 19 = 90, and 7 and 9 are different digits

marks.check: the digits go back into the puzzle
marks.diff: 7 and 9 are marked as different digits

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, put the digits back in the puzzle to check.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Seventy one plus nineteen is ninety, and that matches B zero.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>The two letters hide different digits.

marks.ans: the answer A = 7 and B = 9 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Eigh is seven and B is nine.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum reads seventy one plus nineteen equals ninety.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows A + 1 = 9 and A = 8
marks.carry: the carried 1 is drawn back in above the tens column
marks.fix: the tens column A + 1 + 1 = 9 is written, so A = 7

beats.colours: the struck bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eigh is eight, because eigh plus one should make nine.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But eighty one plus nineteen is one hundred, and the puzzle says ninety.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>Keeko forgot the one that was carried from the units column.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The tens column is eigh plus one plus one, so eigh is seven.
